title: Sky Core Governance keeps control of Spark's most consequential parameters until SPK is judged decentralized enough
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.4 carves the highest-stakes parameters out of Spark Governance for a transitional period: those specified in A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1 (Allocation System Primitive) and A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1 (SparkLend) "will be controlled by Sky Core Governance until Sky determines that the SPK token is decentralized enough to allow for meaningful governance by tokenholders," with the transition "currently estimated for September 17, 2025."

The stated reason is protective: the measure "ensures better decentralization of the SPK token before Spark Governance takes full control." A token whose supply is concentrated is a token whose governance can be captured cheaply, and the parameters at issue are precisely the ones an attacker would want — how capital is allocated and on what terms it is lent.

This produces a real tension with the rest of the Root Edit process. Spark's Artifact specifies an elaborate SPK-holder amendment procedure while the parameters that determine Spark's risk and returns are, for now, not amendable through it. During the transition, Spark Governance is substantially procedural.

The handover condition is also notable for being a judgment rather than a metric. "Decentralized enough" is determined by Sky, with a date offered only as an estimate — so the end of the transition is discretionary, not automatic.
description: Allocation System and SparkLend parameters sit outside Spark Governance during the transition, and Sky decides when the handover happens — initially estimated for September 17, 2025.
